cards.name: Slick Chrome
cards.path: Required/Legacy Styles and More.asl/Legacy Styles and More/All Legacy Default Styles/Web Styles
cards.summary: Liquid-chrome letters: bright white-silver edges with darker grey interior folds, a thin dark rim and a soft drop shadow below. It is built like Mercury (15 px bevel at 75% with the Wow-Chrome gloss and Sharp Highlight contours, its own 120-degree light); the stored differences are the bevel shadow (65% vs 50%), the satin (angle 150 vs 135 degrees, distance 8 vs 7, size 8 vs 11 px), the outline (90% vs 80%), the inner-glow range (30 vs 50) and the contours of the drop shadow, inner shadow and inner glow. Its white inner glow and inner shadow are in Multiply mode and change nothing. The two thumbnails differ by about 4 levels out of 255 over the whole frame but about 27 inside the letters: the same chrome family with the folds and glints in different places. The stored Color Overlay is black, but the render is silver; the picture wins. Effects stored in the style: Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Inner Glow, Bevel & Emboss, Satin, Color Overlay, Stroke.
use_for: chrome music, gaming or sci-fi logo lettering
futuristic poster title
metal-badge heading
avoid: mid-grey grounds: the grey interior merges with them
small type: the folds muddy thin strokes
do not use it together with Mercury as two options: they look much alike
cards.applies_to: a text, shape or pixel layer (not the locked Background layer: double-click it to unlock first). The effects follow the layer's transparency edge, so it reads best on bold type or a solid shape. Effect sizes are in pixels: on a much larger or smaller document use Layer > Layer Style > Scale Effects.
cards.how_to_apply: Styles panel menu > Import Styles... and pick <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Required/Legacy Styles and More.asl (the harvest did not find this style in the panel's default list); 'Slick Chrome' sits in that library (group 'Legacy Styles and More/All Legacy Default Styles/Web Styles'). Then click it with a layer selected. Script: load the file into the style presets (Action Manager set on the application's style list with the file path), then event ASty by panel position.

verified.note: Liquid-chrome letters with white-silver folds, dark grey interior, thin dark rim and a shadow to the lower right; close to Mercury but with the folds and glints in different places (mean difference about 27 levels inside the letters).

review.changes: summary and avoid: the Mercury comparison corrected (bevel shadow 65 vs 50%, satin distance 8 vs 7 and the shadow/glow contours also differ; frame difference 4 levels overall but about 27 inside the letters); the white Multiply inner glow and inner shadow no longer credited with any effect

cards.name: Darker
cards.summary: Mild overall darkening by moving the black input point to 15 (input 15 to 255, output 0 to 255, gamma 1.00): the darkest 15 levels become pure black and the shadows sink by up to 15 levels, an effect that fades toward the highlights, which stay almost unchanged. On the test photo the mean luminance drops from 101 to 91 and the 2nd percentile from 45 to 32, so the mid-tones and the wall look a little deeper with no colour shift.
use_for: taking the edge off a slightly bright or washed-out photo
deepening blacks a little before sharpening
quick darker variant of an exposure
avoid: the darkest 15 levels clip to black, so dark suits and hair lose detail on dim photos
it does not add contrast to a flat image: use Increase Contrast 1 to 3
strong darkening: Midtones Darker lowers the mean further without clipping
cards.applies_to: a colour or greyscale image layer or document; as a Levels adjustment layer it changes everything visible below it (clip it to one layer to limit it), and Image > Adjustments > Levels applies it destructively to the selected pixel layer. The file sets the composite (RGB) channel only; the red, green and blue channel entries are left at their defaults (0 to 255, gamma 1.00).
cards.how_to_apply: Usual route (not exercised by the harvest): Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Levels, then choose 'Darker' from the Preset menu in Properties (Photoshop lists the shipped presets by file name), or use Load Preset... and pick <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Presets/Levels/Darker.alv. Script: the Action Manager event levels with using set to that .alv file, which is how PGD applied it on a scratch document (read-back confirmed).
cards.notes: Values read from the shipped .alv file (a binary Levels preset decoded structurally); the look comes from PGD's thumbnail, where the preset was applied by script to the test photo (result on top, untouched photo below), with luminance statistics measured on the two halves of that thumbnail (Rec. 601 luma; original mean 101, 2nd percentile 45, 98th percentile 208).

verified.note: Result half visibly a little darker than the original; measured luma mean 102.7 to 93.2, 2nd percentile 45 to 32 (same crop both halves). Decoded .alv (all 29 records plus the Lvls tail) changes only the composite record; applying that curve to the bottom half reproduces the top half's luma within 0.5 level.

cards.name: Increase Contrast 1
cards.summary: The gentlest contrast boost: black input point 10 and white input point 245 (input 10 to 245, output 0 to 255, gamma 1.00), so the darkest and lightest 10 levels clip and the range between is stretched. On the test photo the 2nd percentile moves 45 to 38 and the 98th 208 to 214, the mean 101 to 98; the picture looks slightly crisper.
use_for: lifting a flat or hazy photo a little
quick punch before sharpening
subtle contrast for web images
avoid: clips 10 levels at each end, so very dark or bright detail is lost
it is the mildest of the three: use Increase Contrast 2 or 3 for more
it does not fix colour casts
